2610.13059.title: CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation
2610.13059.paper_summary: Radiology reports are essential for diagnostic reasoning and patient care, yet their manual preparation is time-consuming and cognitively demanding. Automatic radiology report generation (RRG) offers a scalable alternative, but existing models often produce lengthy, unstructured narratives that overlook diagnostic cues and multi-view information. We present Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation (CliQ-RRG), a unified two-stage framework for interpretable and clinically grounded reporting. In Stage 1, CliQ-RRG employs a Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment module that aligns image and text representations using predicted disease embeddings, reinforced by a Prior-Guided Attention Module (PrAM) to capture multi-view dependencies across current and prior scans. In Stage 2, GraphRAG-guided retrieval augments intermediate textual representations with graph-grounded clinical evidence, and a large language model restructures them into concise, interpretable question-answer (QA) pairs with diagnostic summaries. Experiments on two public chest X-ray benchmarks demonstrate that CliQ-RRG consistently outperforms prior methods across both lexical and clinical metrics, generating accurate and clinically coherent QA-style radiology reports. Code is available at: https://github.com/chandravardhan-singh-raghaw/CliQ-RRG.
2610.13059.paper_summary_zh: 放射學報告對於診斷推理和病人護理至關重要，但其手動準備耗時且認知負擔重。自動放射學報告生成（RRG）提供了一種可擴展的替代方案，但現有模型往往產生冗長且無結構的敘述，忽略了診斷線索和多視角信息。我們提出了臨床知識引導的疾病感知視覺-文本對齊用於問答風格放射學報告生成（CliQ-RRG），這是一個統一的兩階段框架，用於可解釋且臨床基礎的報告。在第一階段，CliQ-RRG採用疾病感知視覺-文本對齊模塊，通過預測的疾病嵌入對圖像和文本表示進行對齊，並由先驗引導注意模塊（PrAM）強化，以捕捉當前和先前掃描之間的多視角依賴性。在第二階段，GraphRAG引導的檢索用圖形基礎的臨床證據增強中間文本表示，大型語言模型將其重構為簡潔、可解釋的問答（QA）對，並附上診斷摘要。在兩個公共胸部X光基準上的實驗顯示，CliQ-RRG在詞彙和臨床指標上始終優於先前的方法，生成準確且臨床連貫的問答風格放射學報告。代碼可在以下網址獲得：https://github.com/chandravardhan-singh-raghaw/CliQ-RRG。
